definition: The process by which regulatory bodies and governance institutions are co-opted by the entities they are meant to regulate. In AI governance, this manifests as industry dominance of standard-setting, revolving-door appointments, and framing regulatory agendas around industry interests.
rationale_for_coinage: Skeptics see institutional capture as a primary mechanism by which AI governance fails. Both accelerationists and safetyists may use 'capture' but frame it differently — accelerationists see government overreach as the capture problem, safetyists focus on inadequate regulation rather than captured regulation.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Governance oversight is the intended function of regulation; institutional capture is the failure mode where that function is subverted.

contested_aspects: Whether industry participation in regulation is inherently capture or necessary expertise
Whether capture is avoidable in technically complex domains
